clue.text: Birds turned up on roof of reprocessing plant

parts.note: larks are songbirds

indicators.note: turned says the little word up is flipped round to read backwards
in a down clue the roof of a word is its top, so its first letter

explanation.surface: Birds have come to perch upside down on top of a recycling plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' looks like part of the factory picture, but it is the definition. In a down answer 'on' puts the reversed UP below LARKS, then R tops off the grid entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Larkspur is a garden flower, the delphinium relative, so a kind of plant.

clue.text: Act indecently? I become tight-lipped

indicators.note: acting indecently means behaving improperly, so the letters of act are disordered

parts.note: to turn, as milk turns sour, is to become

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether their act is indecent and resolves to say nothing more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'indecently' rearranges ACT into TAC.
explanation.definitionFit: Taciturn describes a reserved person who speaks little, which is what tight-lipped means.

clue.text: Name of composer heard

indicators.note: heard says the word is the spoken version of another word with a different spelling

parts.note: Handel is the German-born composer of Messiah

explanation.surface: Someone hears the name of a composer mentioned.
explanation.definitionFit: A handle is slang for a person's name or nickname, as in a radio call sign.

clue.text: Richly seasoned stew shown in red-top abroad

parts.note: a red-top is a British tabloid newspaper, disparagingly called a rag
abroad can mean out and about, out of doors

explanation.surface: A tabloid shows a lavish foreign stew in its pages.
explanation.walkthrough: A red-top is a British tabloid, named for its red masthead; such papers are dismissively called rags.
explanation.definitionFit: A ragout is a French-style stew of meat and vegetables, heavily seasoned.

clue.text: Traveller's passage — cost of passage ending in Dover

parts.note: a way is a route or passage
a fare is what one pays for a journey

indicators.note: the ending of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A traveller pays for a crossing that finishes at Dover.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-s stands for 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A wayfarer is someone journeying on foot, a traveller.

clue.text: Brief film entertaining wife

indicators.note: to entertain is to hold or host, so one word takes the other within it

parts.note: a film is a thin layer, as of dust

explanation.surface: A short movie shows a married woman being entertained.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brief' looks like an adjective about the film; it is the noun, slang for a barrister.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a brief is a lawyer, from the brief of instructions a barrister receives.

clue.text: Bail out a mostly wicked pantomime character

indicators.note: out here means wrong or disordered, so the letters of bail are rearranged
mostly means almost all of the word, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: bad means wicked

explanation.surface: A villain in a pantomime gets bailed out of trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bail out' rearranges BAIL as ALIB, and 'mostly' trims BAD to BA. A pantomime is a British Christmas stage show built on fairy tales.
explanation.definitionFit: Ali Baba, of the forty thieves, is a stock hero of British Christmas pantomime.

clue.text: Boy's from Pisa, actually

indicators.note: from says the answer is taken out of the letters of the next words, spanning both

explanation.surface: A lad claims he really does come from the Italian city of Pisa.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-s is 'is', linking definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Isaac is a boy's given name, so a boy may be called that.

clue.text: Magnificent article about a Spanish city

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: grand means magnificent
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A splendid piece of writing about a city in Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: Granada is an Andalusian city, home of the Alhambra palace.

clue.text: Progressive Indian state leader

parts.note: Goa is a state on India's west coast
a head is a leader

explanation.surface: A forward-thinking chief minister of an Indian state.
explanation.definitionFit: Go-ahead as an adjective describes someone enterprising and forward-looking.

clue.text: Belonging to Gurkha, kitbag and military material

indicators.note: Belonging to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Khaki items belong to a Gurkha's kitbag along with his military kit.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition included 'and', which is only the link joining wordplay to definition; 'military material' alone defines the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Khaki is the drab cloth used for army uniforms.

clue.text: Insect in Spooner's large jug, empty

indicators.note: Spooner's says the opening sounds of two words are swapped, after the famously muddled Reverend Spooner

parts.note: a flagon is a large jug for drink
dry means empty, as a dry well

explanation.surface: An insect has fallen into a big jug that has been drained.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the openings of FLAGON DRY gives DRAGON FLY.
explanation.definitionFit: A dragonfly is a long-bodied flying insect found near water.

clue.text: Might one help one see painting in a different light?

definitions.text: Might one help one see painting in a different light?

parts.words: Might one help one see painting in a different light?
parts.note: to see something in a different light means to change one's view of it; literally, cleaning a canvas changes how the paint looks

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom about changing one's opinion becomes literal: removing old varnish makes a canvas look brighter.
explanation.definitionFit: A conservator who cleans and repairs old paintings literally changes how they look.

clue.text: Income level in Parisian's street

indicators.note: in says one word sits inside the other

parts.note: rue is French for street
even means level

explanation.surface: A Parisian's earnings depend on what level of street they live in.
explanation.definitionFit: Revenue is money coming in, such as a business's or state's income.

clue.text: Leave shortly, heading for India on holiday

indicators.note: shortly says the word is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: to vacate is to leave a place

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone will soon take leave and fly off to India for a break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on holiday' reads as one phrase, but 'on' is wordplay and 'holiday' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Vacation is the American word for a holiday, and also a break between university terms.

clue.text: Perfect example in eastern religious book

parts.note: pi is informal British for pious or religious
a tome is a large book

explanation.surface: A model specimen found in an Eastern holy scripture.
explanation.walkthrough: PI is British slang, short for pious.
explanation.definitionFit: An epitome is a person or thing that typifies a quality perfectly.

clue.text: Strange code, strange etiquette

indicators.note: something strange is out of its normal form, so the letters of code are jumbled

parts.note: rum is old British slang for odd or strange

explanation.surface: An odd code of conduct makes for odd manners.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'Strange' rearranges CODE as DECO; the second gives RUM.
explanation.definitionFit: Decorum is proper, polite behaviour, which is what etiquette prescribes.

clue.text: Where there may be lots of holidaymakers affected by it in south-east

definitions.text: Where there may be lots of holidaymakers

parts.note: camp means affected or theatrical in manner

indicators.note: in says one piece sits inside the other

explanation.surface: South-east resorts are full of holidaymakers who are affected by something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lots' hints at plots, the pitches holidaymakers rent.
explanation.definitionFit: A campsite is a field with pitches where many tourists stay in tents.

clue.text: Rodent had got loose inside, causing scene of utter confusion

indicators.note: inside says the jumbled piece goes within the other word

parts.note: a mouse is a rodent

indicators.note: got loose suggests letters breaking free and scattering, so had is rearranged

explanation.surface: A mouse escaped indoors and caused chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a mouse running free indoors, but 'got loose' is the anagram signal, scrambling the little word into ADH.
explanation.definitionFit: A madhouse, literally an asylum, is idiomatically any place of chaos.

clue.text: Back home, give orders to deputy

parts.note: to second a proposal is to back it
in means at home
to command is to give orders

explanation.surface: Someone returns home and starts ordering a subordinate about.
explanation.definitionFit: The second-in-command is the officer ranking just below the leader, a deputy.

clue.text: Top two maidens in action

indicators.note: in says one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a suit is a legal action
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over, so two make MM

explanation.surface: The top pair of maidens are seen in action.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a maiden is an over in which no runs are scored; scorecards write it M.
explanation.definitionFit: A summit is the highest point, the top of a mountain.

clue.text: Most certainly not involving king and country

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: no way is an emphatic refusal
R is the abbreviation for rex, king

explanation.surface: A firm refusal to involve the monarch and the nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Norway is a Scandinavian nation, a country.

clue.text: About time to get down for short sleep

parts.note: ca is short for circa, about
nap is the soft raised surface of cloth, like down

explanation.surface: It's about time to lie down for a quick doze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get down' suggests lying down, but 'down' is fluff, giving NAP.
explanation.definitionFit: A catnap is a brief light sleep, a short sleep.

clue.text: Established rule in Isle of Man following a vote

indicators.note: following says the island piece comes after the others

parts.note: X is the mark made on a ballot paper

explanation.surface: A rule made law in the Isle of Man after a ballot.
explanation.walkthrough: The Isle of Man is a self-governing island in the Irish Sea, abbreviated IOM.
explanation.definitionFit: An axiom is a principle accepted as true, an established rule.

clue.text: Moment to abort abnormal launch?

indicators.note: abnormal means not in the usual form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rocket launch is aborted at the last moment because something is wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'launch' suggests a rocket, but here it is a boat. 'abnormal' rearranges TO ABORT as TORBOAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A launch is a large motor-driven pleasure boat.

clue.text: Extremely small, I leave Irish port

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: to go is to leave

explanation.surface: A small person announces they are leaving an Irish harbour town.
explanation.definitionFit: Sligo is a town and port on the north-west coast of Ireland.

clue.text: Very behindhand after electric current cut off

indicators.note: after puts the very late part following the current

parts.note: I is the physics symbol for electric current
so means very
late means behindhand

explanation.surface: Someone running very late after the power was cut.
explanation.definitionFit: To isolate is to separate or set apart, as a community cut off by floods.

clue.text: Occasionally employed by rival newspaper?

definitions.meaning: working at The Times, a rival of the Telegraph

explanation.walkthrough: The Times is a London daily, the Telegraph's long-time competitor.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone on the staff of The Times works there, so is literally at the paper.
